name: Iris Fila
author: E. T. Carter
description: A filament-halo iris filling the frame: hundreds of hair-thin luminous strands radiate from a soft glowing core, each with a hashed length so the field feathers like a nebula or a dandelion clock rather than reading as solid spokes. No hard pupil here, the centre blooms bright; the strands are brightest mid-field and feather into a faint halo at the edges, shimmering on per-strand phases.

params.label: Strands
params.effect: Number of hair-thin strands around the circle; fewer reads as distinct filaments, more as a silken luminous haze.

params.label: Feather
params.effect: How much the strand lengths vary; 0 gives an even disc, 1 a ragged feathered halo of long and short filaments.

params.label: Drift
params.effect: Rate at which strands shimmer and wander on their own phases; 0 holds the halo still, higher makes it twinkle.

params.label: Core glow
params.effect: Radius of the soft luminous core the strands radiate from; larger floods more of the centre with bloom.
